node.label: Émile Durkheim
node.date_label: 1893: De la division du travail social · 1895: Les Règles de la méthode sociologique · 1912: Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse
node.description: A sociologist whose work makes collective institutions, obligations and representations objects of causal inquiry. His methodological writings distinguish external and constraining social facts from their mere frequency, and distinguish the causes of institutions from the functions they later serve.
node.representative_figures_and_works: De la division du travail social (1893); Les Règles de la méthode sociologique (1895); Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse (1912).
node.scope_note: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.

proposed_edges.relationship: Defines social facts through externality and constraining force, rather than mere prevalence among individuals.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own chapter I opening read, including obligations, conventions and currents. His examples are attributed illustrations, not independently tested universal laws.

proposed_edges.relationship: Separates the causal explanation of institutions from their utility or present functions.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own chapter V section I opening read; changed uses and institutional survivals challenge explanation by usefulness alone. This is a methodological resource, without claiming every comparative historian accepted it.
